title: Launch smoke-run checklist & PRD riffnotes
body:
Morning rapid log (short, messy)

Context: final smoke run for hosted-api v2 rollout. Goal = validate traffic routing, observe latency tail, confirm fallback to smaller model variant works, final PRD edits locked before posting.

Top priorities (today):
- [ ] Run 8:30am smoke with internal traffic (route=canary-10%) -> watch 99th pct latency, error spikes (INF-341).
- [ ] Confirm rollout policy: canary -> 50% -> 100% (auto rollback threshold 3errors/min or +50% tail lat).
- [ ] Merge PRD small wording updates (section "fallback policy" + example traffic policy). See inline comments below.
- [ ] Quick sync with SRE & infra at 9:00 (Evan) re: autoscaler warmup for dedicated pools.
- [ ] Send short status note to sales/solutions 10:30am: "initial canary green / next window at 11:30"

PRD edits (notes to self / inline fragments)
- Why we need "graceful degrade" section: customer story where higher-latency model allowed UX to continue with a short notice banner. Add one sentence + example JSON policy.
- Expand "observability" paragraph: call out token-level cost dashboard and per-route 99p latency. Add link to confluence page.
- Remove TODO in "API examples" — swap placeholder example with real SDK snippet (use python snippet from github/prs/482).

Open questions (to follow up)
- Sophie: can we reduce default batch window from 12ms -> 8ms for chat endpoints without hurting throughput? (ticket LR-872)
- Legal: do we need an explicit data retention mention for private deployments? (ask Kate)
- Is there appetite for a short "migration guide" for customers pinning model versions? (put as small appendix)

Quick checklist for smoke run (detailed)
- Pre-run (15m):
  - confirm canary config loaded (console: /routes/hosted-api/canary)
  - ensure monitoring alerts unmuted for this window
  - create ephemeral load generator job (note: use labs/gensmoke v1.3)
- Run (0-20m):
  - ramp to 10% traffic in 2m, hold 5m, observe 99p and error rate
  - AWS spot events? check infra console
  - verify fallback: kill one GPU node in staging variant, ensure failure route triggers fallback model variant and no client errors
- Post-run (20-40m):
  - collect trace sample (open trace ids in issue INF-341)
  - capture token-cost breakdown snapshot (console->costs->token-breakdown)
  - quick retro notes + escalate anything > 2% error to SRE

Stakeholder follow-ups (short messages to send)
- To @eng-sre (Evan): "If we see sustained 99p increase > 200ms during canary, pause rollout and hold for diagnostics. Keep autoscaler manual for next window."
- To @solutions (Claire): "Initial canary tomorrow 10:30am; we'll flag if any customers in early access need to be rescheduled."
- To @legal (Kate): "Quick Q: do we need new language in PRD about customer-managed KMS keys for private installs?"

Notes & stray thoughts (for later cleanup)
- Performance note: observed a small KV cache miss spike when sequence length exceeded 1024 — might be related to new tokenizer change. Add to infra retro.
- Consider adding a one-pager for customers: "What to expect during a canary" (bullet list + timeline).
- If canary flaps twice, run emergency rollback playbook (link: slack:#launch-runbook -> msg pinned).

Short action log (timestamps to fill after):
- 08:15 prep done (load job created)
- 08:40 observed 0.8% errors during ramp -> paused -> diag started
- 09:05 infra fixed node drain issue -> resumed at 09:12

TODOs (personal)
- finish PRD language + push commit to github by EOD
- schedule 30m follow-up with Sophie next week to lock batching defaults
- export cost snapshot and attach to JIRA INF-341

End messy notes. Will clean into PRD and post to confluence after 2nd smoke green.

-- Maya
